security_audit.summary: Nineteen findings are confirmed because command examples invoke the unpinned claude-flow package through npx, which may download and execute external code. The remaining findings are Markdown delimiters, inline labels, JavaScript examples, or documentation links and are false positives. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin every npx claude-flow example to a reviewed version, and state that users must approve network downloads before execution.
Add warnings and backup steps before force initialization, memory clearing, session imports, session stops, or other state-changing operations.

content.user_title: Coordinate Advanced Claude Flow Agent Swarms
content.value_statement: Complex projects require coordinated agents, durable context, and transparent decisions. This skill guides Claude Flow swarms through queen-led roles, consensus, memory, and sessions.
actual_capabilities: Guides hive initialization, swarm spawning, status checks, metrics, and memory monitoring.
Explains strategic, tactical, and adaptive queen roles with specialized worker assignments.
Covers majority, weighted, and Byzantine consensus strategies for collective decisions.
Documents session creation, pause, resume, stop, checkpoint, export, and import workflows.
Shows collective memory storage, retrieval, search, association, configuration, and optimization patterns.
Provides integration examples for Claude Code, SPARC workflows, repositories, and pull request reviews.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples; the separate claude-flow runtime performs all orchestration.
Command examples use npx, which may download packages, access repositories, and modify local state.
Performance and benchmark claims are not independently validated within the skill.
API snippets omit imports, validation, and error handling, so projects require adaptation.

use_cases.title: Plan a distributed implementation
use_cases.description: Define queen strategy, worker specialties, task ownership, and consensus gates for a complex software project.

use_cases.title: Coordinate delivery and review
use_cases.description: Organize parallel implementation, testing, security review, documentation, and release decisions across specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Operate persistent agent sessions
use_cases.description: Monitor sessions, preserve checkpoints, inspect memory, and tune worker capacity for repeated research or development work.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic hive
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a basic hive mind for [objective]. Recommend a queen type, four worker roles, initialization steps, and status checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a clearly scoped project

prompt_templates.title: Design a delivery swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Claude Flow swarm for [project]. Assign specialized workers, dependencies, checkpoints, and a suitable consensus strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a stalled session
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this stalled hive session: [symptoms]. Propose safe status, metrics, memory, checkpoint, and resume steps without clearing data.

prompt_templates.title: Engineer a multi-hive workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced multi-hive plan for [program]. Define shared memory, Byzantine decisions, scaling thresholds, failure recovery, and measurable review gates.

output_examples.input: Plan a swarm to build an authenticated REST API.
output_examples.output: Use a tactical queen with backend, database, security, testing, and documentation workers. Require weighted consensus at architecture and release checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Recover a paused research session without losing findings.
output_examples.output: Inspect session status and memory first. Verify the latest checkpoint, resume the selected session, then monitor metrics before assigning new tasks.

output_examples.input: Coordinate frontend and backend work as separate hives.
output_examples.output: Create named frontend and backend hives with shared memory keys. Use interface checkpoints and consensus reviews before integration testing.

best_practices: Match the queen type to the objective before selecting worker count or consensus rules.
Create checkpoints before state-changing operations and monitor status, metrics, and memory throughout execution.
Pin reviewed package versions and inspect generated commands before allowing external execution.
anti_patterns: Do not spawn many workers without clear roles, dependencies, and completion criteria.
Do not clear memory, force initialization, or import sessions without a verified backup.
Do not use consensus as a substitute for tests, security review, or accountable human decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Claude Flow runtime?
faq.answer: No. It documents Claude Flow workflows and APIs, while the runtime must be installed and executed separately.

faq.question: Which queen type should I choose?
faq.answer: Use strategic for planning, tactical for implementation, and adaptive for changing or optimization-focused work.

faq.question: Which consensus methods are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers majority voting, queen-weighted voting, and Byzantine consensus requiring a two-thirds majority.

faq.question: Can sessions continue after interruption?
faq.answer: The documented workflows support checkpoints, pause, resume, export, and import when the installed runtime provides these features.

faq.question: Does the skill access the network?
faq.answer: The Markdown itself does not. Its unpinned npx commands may download packages, and repository workflows may access remote services.

faq.question: Are the command examples safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review package versions, arguments, repository access, backups, and state-changing flags before execution.
